enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1012 PM MST Sun Nov 1 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 921 PM MST Sun Nov 1 2026

 - Showers and thunderstorms will end overnight with periods of 
   moderate rainfall and strong winds possible. 

 - Drier weather with breezy to windy conditions will occur 
   Monday with stronger winds in the Sacramento Mountains where 
   damaging wind gusts up to 70 mph may occur along the east 
   slopes. 

 - Quieter and drier weather will prevail after Monday with light
   winds and temperatures remaining seasonable. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 921 PM MST Sun Nov 1 2026

Active weather will continue for a few more hours this evening
then begin taper off and dissipate in the early morning hours.
The band of showers and weak embedded thunderstorms is associated
with a strong Pacific front that is part of a larger weather
system moving from west to east across the region. After the
passage of the frontal system, conditions will turn dry and breezy
to windy for the lowlands throughout the day on Monday. 

Stronger winds aloft will generate very strong winds along the 
east slopes of the Sacramento mountains in the early morning hours
through mid day. Wind gusts up to 70 mph may occur along the east
slopes of the Sacramento Mountains. A high wind warning is in 
effect for that area. Temperatures will also be cooler behind the 
front with lowland temperatures in the upper 60s to 70 degrees. 
Tuesday will also be cooler but a mild warming trend will occur by
mid week. 

An extended period of quieter dry weather will occur the rest of
the week and into next weekend. Predominately westerly flow 
pattern aloft will be in place. Low pressure troughs and short 
wave ridges will transit through the region with little impact on 
southern New Mexico and far west Texas. The westerly flow breaks 
down next weekend and is replaced by strong ridge that will 
maintain the dry pattern for the region. Tuesday through Sunday 
will be mostly sunny, with light winds and seasonal temperatures. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 921 PM MST Sun Nov 1 2026

A Pacific frontal boundary with band of showers with embedded 
thunderstorms continues to from west to east across Southern New 
Mexico and Far West Texas. As of 05Z shower activity is tapering 
off at KTCS and KDMN. Showers remain possible for KLRU and KELP 
for the next couple of hours before ending around 07Z. There are 
low ceilings associated with this band of weather that will lift 
shortly after passing the through the region. Breezy west winds
of 15 to 20 knots will fill in behind the system as skies 
gradually clear. Winds over the mountain ranges will be strong
with wind warnings in effect for the Sacramento Mountains for
Monday. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 9215 PM MST Sun Nov 1 2026

No fire weather concerns are forecast through the period. Showers
and thunderstorms have ended over southwestern New Mexico and 
will soon end over south central New Mexico by early morning. 
Monday's weather will remain somewhat active with brief isolated
showers over the Gila Region and breezy to windy conditions, 
especially along east facing slopes. The strongest winds are 
expected over the Sacramento mountains where wind gusts could 
exceed 50 mph along the east slopes. While wind speeds may exceed 
critical thresholds, RH values will remain high in the 30 to 50 
percent range. Winds will subside on Tuesday and remain light for
the remainder of the week. Dry conditions with temperatures near
seasonal are expected. Vent rates will be in the good to excellent
range for Monday then become poor with the lighter winds on
Tuesday. 

&&
